### Demonstrations (hermetic; `env -i`, scratch; **no real booked scope, no host probe**)
- **In-scope stop (control K):** stubs `scope_gate` to SUCCEED and arms `bash` (the one command `child()` uses to spawn a run child) as a tripwire, then invokes `self_test`. The guard must refuse **before any child dispatch**, so the tripwire file is **absent** → no child → run-mode fetch/build (which live only behind the L692 gate inside that child) are **unreachable**. Result: rc 2 + the refusal reason + no SELF_TEST=PASS + no tripwire. GREEN.
- **Out-of-scope normal behavior:** clean `--self-test` PASS rc 0 (guard correctly silent); `--limitations` rc 0; self-test PASS by absolute and relative path; 0 environment-default leaks; 33 readonly pins intact.
- **Guard-removal inversion:** disabling the top guard makes control (K) go **RED** (`reason=guardprobe`) — the forced-scope self-test proceeds and a child spawns (tripwire fires). So the guard is behaviorally load-bearing, not a grep.
- **No regression:** the full v13 inversion matrix reproduces 11/11 RED (mkdir -p / install -d / mkdir ${OUT} before gate; neuter run-guard → selfabort+verifyabort; unknown→run; drop HUP/TERM/INT/EXIT traps; never-fired TERM → trap-term).

### Assumptions stated honestly (keen-otter)
- `self_test`'s ONLY external surface is `child()` (`bash "$SELF"`); there is no direct git/curl/wget/cargo/npm/http/clone/admit/exec in `self_test`, and run-mode fetch/build (`git init/remote add`, shallow fetch, build) exist ONLY after the L692 scope gate inside a run child. Hence intercepting `bash` + the top guard bounds every workload path from `--self-test`.
- The in-scope condition is demonstrated by a **stubbed** `scope_gate` (a real booked cgroup / host probe is not authorized). The guard's real-cgroup correctness is **by construction** — it calls the very same `scope_gate` the run preamble relies on — and is exercised by stub, not by an actual in-scope cgroup. I do NOT claim universal hermeticity beyond this: the guard ensures no `--self-test` workload path given the verified fact that fetch/build are reachable only via a gated run child.
- A run child, even if ever spawned, is itself out-of-scope (reads its own /proc/self/cgroup), so fetch/build stay unreachable in the ordinary envelope regardless.
